Step 1: the white vehicle base (b1, the model's first piece, rests_on []) is shown with one black 2x3 plate (b2) already on one end. The second black 2x3 plate (b3) is added on the other end. The page does not say which plate was placed first.

Both plates sit on the recessed 2-wide end platforms of the base, with their bottoms clutching the studs there. Specific stud port names are not given because I could not identify them reliably from the illustration, so the edges leave the ports null.
Studs and anti-studs are interlocking, so each plate-to-base connection is a single joined edge (push-on, rigid, reversible by hand). b2 and b3 rest_on b1.

Step 2: two dark gray 2x2 wheel-holder plates (lego-6157) go on the black 2x3 plates, one at each end. b4 is on b2 and b5 is on b3. The drawing does not show which of the two black plates is b2 and which is b3, so the pairing is an assumption.
Each holder sits on the end of its black plate, toward the outside of the car. Specific stud ports are not identifiable from the drawing, so the ports are null.
The wheel holders are on the end platforms and do not appear to clutch the base itself, so rests_on lists only the black plate.

Step 3: the chassis (b1 with b2-b5) is turned over. The base studs are now on top and the wheel holders point down. The red steering stand b6 is pressed onto two studs of the base's left raised section, next to the recessed center.
The stand's two studs are not identified in the drawing, so the ports are null. b6 rests_on b1 only.

Step 4: four white wheel arches go over the wheel holders, two at each end of the chassis, one per side. b7 and b8 are at the left (front-left) end and b9 and b10 at the right end. The drawing does not make clear which arch is which, so this assignment is my choice.

Each arch's 2x2 plate is pressed onto studs of the base. Specific ports are null. All four rest_on b1. The arches also sit over the wheel holders b4 and b5 but do not clutch them, so they are not listed in rests_on.

Step 5 builds a front-end sub-assembly in the inset, then fits it on the car's front end (the end with the nearer arches, which I take to be b7 and b8). Inset 1: white 52038 (b11). Inset 2: grille tile 2412b (b12) goes on the two studs on its front face. Inset 3: two trans-yellow cheese slopes (b13, b14) go on the studs either side of the grille, as headlights.
b12, b13 and b14 are attached to the side of b11 (studs facing the front), not stacked on top of it. They are recorded as joined edges to b11.
The sub-assembly is fixed to the front of the chassis. Whether it clutches b1, b7 and b8 or only some of them is not clear from the drawing. I recorded all three, with null ports, as an assumption.
I identified the white piece as lego-52038 from its shape and the parts list. No other white part fits.

Step 6 repeats the step 5 pattern at the rear. Inset 1: a second white 52038 (b15). Inset 2: a white tile (b16) goes between the two side studs on the rear face. Inset 3: two trans-red cheese slopes (b17, b18) go either side of the tile, as tail lights. The sub-assembly then attaches to the rear end of the chassis, between arches b9 and b10.
The white middle piece in inset 2 is taken to be a white 1 x 2 tile with groove (lego-3069b), because the parts list has white 3069b and nothing else fits.
The tile and slopes are attached to the side of b15, as with the front end in step 5. Which chassis pieces b15 clutches (b1, b9, b10) is an assumption. All ports are null.

Step 7: a red 3x4 wedge plate (b19) goes on the front as the hood. It covers the studs of front block b11 and of the front arches b7 and b8. A red 1x4 brick (b20) goes on the base's raised rear section, just in front of the rear block b15.

Which pieces the wedge clutches is read from the drawing: b11, b7, b8. The red 1x4 brick appears to sit on base studs only, so it rests_on b1 alone. If it also overlaps the rear arch plates b9 or b10, that is not clear in the drawing. All ports are null.

Step 8 is marked 2x. Each of the two red cupboards (b21, b22) gets a white door (b23, b24) hinged into the open side, as the green arrows show. The two cupboards go on the rear of the car, one on each side, with the doors facing outward.
Which door goes with which cupboard, and which side each cupboard is on, is not stated. I paired b21 with b23 and b22 with b24, and put b21 on the b9 side and b22 on the b10 side.

The cupboards' bottoms clutch the rear block b15 and the rear arch plates. The drawing doesn't make the exact overlap clear, so this is an assumption. The red brick b20 from step 7 is not clearly visible under or beside the cupboards, so I did not add it to rests_on. Ports are null except the door hinges.
Step 9: the trans-light blue windscreen (b25) is pressed onto the cab area behind the hood, in front of the rear cupboards.
Which pieces it clutches is read from the drawing and is an assumption. I listed the hood wedge b19, the red brick b20 and the base b1. Ports are null.

Step 10 inset: a stack of three plates, built from the bottom up. The bottom is a trans-dark blue 1x2 plate (b28), then a white 1x2 plate (b29), then a black 1x2 plate with door rail (b30). The stack goes on the roof of the rear cupboards, in the gap between the two white strips. It is the ambulance's light.

Two white 1x4 tiles (b26, b27) appear on the roof edges of the cupboards in the main drawing but have no callout and were not on the previous page. I recorded them as added in this step: b26 on cupboard b21 and b27 on cupboard b22. This is my reading of the drawing.

The light stack (b28) is taken to straddle both cupboards in the gap between the tiles. This and the cupboard-to-tile pairing are assumptions, and all ports are null. The trans-dark blue plate looks light blue in the drawing, but the parts list only has trans-dark blue 1x2 plates.

Step 11 has no callout box. Two new pieces show in the main drawing. The first is a white roof piece with two studs on top. It is identified as lego-45677 (the curved wedged brick with 2 studs) from the parts list. It covers the cab and rests on the windscreen b25. I also listed the rear white block b15 as support, which is an assumption.

The second piece is a black lever (lego-298c02), at the rear in the gap between the white tiles. I put its base on the studs of cupboard b21. It might instead be on b22, or on the stack in the gap, which the drawing doesn't settle. Ports are null.

Step 12 has no callout for the wheels, but all four wheels with tyres appear on the car, so I added them here. Each white wheel (6014b) fits on a wheel-holder pin of b4 or b5 and turns freely. Each black tyre (6015) is fitted on its wheel. Which wheel is on which holder end is an assumption: b33 and b34 on b4, b35 and b36 on b5. The holder pins have no port in the catalogue, so the holder port is null.

Third, a white 1x2 tile (b45) goes on the blue plate. The bar then sits on the roof at the back edge. I assume it clutches the roof studs of b31 only, and the ports are null.

Step 13: the medical-symbol stickers go on the roof (b31) and on both cupboard doors (b23, b24). The sticker sheet (lego-55073) is one piece in the parts list, so it is recorded once and joined to all three surfaces.

I am keeping the three groups. This is not a real error in the manual. The booklet builds the car in steps 1-12 (plus the stickers in step 13). In step 13 it also builds two loose accessories for the doctor, and the car is not attached to either of them. The first is the hand-held medical device (b47, b48, b49). The second is the briefcase (b50), carried in the doctor's other hand.

The doctor stands beside the car in the final picture and holds both accessories. He is a minifigure, and the official parts list does not include minifigure pieces. I did not add him as a node, since that would add parts the list doesn't have. Adding a joined or contact edge from the accessories to the car would invent a connection the booklet does not show.
